# v1.4.1 — Installers for every platform, and the shortcuts that 1.4.0 promised

A corrective release. 1.4.0 shipped with Linux installers only, and its tag was cut just before the keyboard shortcuts its own notes described. Both are fixed here. **If you're on 1.4.0, this is the build you want** — nothing else about the app changed.

---

## 📦 Six installers, built on the machine each one needs

Until now the release carried whatever a single Linux machine could produce. Every target is now built on a runner that can actually produce it, so all six ship together:

| Platform | Installers |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 | `.deb` · `.rpm` · `.AppImage` |
| Linux arm64 | `.deb` · `.rpm` · `.AppImage` |
| Windows x64 | `.exe` (NSIS) · `.msi` |
| Windows arm64 | `.exe` (NSIS) |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `.dmg` |
| macOS Intel | `.dmg` |

**arm64 is new** on all three platforms. Windows arm64 has no `.msi` because WiX, the tool that builds it, doesn't support that architecture.

Locally, `bun run app:build --list` now tells you which of those your machine can produce and why it can't produce the rest, and `--target` builds just one.

---

## ⌨️ Keyboard navigation

Described in the 1.4.0 notes, but it landed after that tag was cut. It's here now.

| | |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+H` | Home |
| `Ctrl+E` | Sessions |
| `Ctrl+K` | Skills |
| `Ctrl+M` | Marketplace |
| `Ctrl+G` | Settings |
| `Ctrl+Tab` · `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | Next / previous tab, wrapping at both ends |

**Each section shortcut is a toggle**: already in Marketplace, `Ctrl+M` takes you back to your terminal.

They work while you're typing inside an agent, which is the point — and that has a price worth stating. `Ctrl+M` *is* Enter and `Ctrl+H` *is* Backspace at the terminal level, and `Ctrl+E` / `Ctrl+K` are readline editing keys; those four stop reaching the agent. Enter and Backspace have their own keys and still work; what you lose is emacs-style editing. The list and this caveat live in **Settings → Keyboard shortcuts**.

---

## 📥 Which file do I want?

| You're on | Download |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu / Debian | `.deb` — `amd64` for a normal PC, `arm64` for ARM |
| Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE | `.rpm` — `x86_64` or `aarch64` |
| Any other Linux | `.AppImage` — `amd64` or `aarch64`; `chmod +x` and run it |
| Windows | `.exe` — the `.msi` is there for deployment tooling |
| Mac, M1 and newer | the `aarch64` `.dmg` |
| Mac, Intel | the `x64` `.dmg` |

On Linux the same machine is called different things by different packagers: a normal 64-bit PC is `amd64` in the `.deb` and the AppImage but `x86_64` in the `.rpm`, and an ARM one is `arm64` in the `.deb` but `aarch64` in the other two. Pick the row, not the word.

The macOS builds are unsigned, so Gatekeeper will stop the first launch: right-click the app → **Open** → Open.

Everything from [1.4.0](https://github.com/luis3132/ControlCode/releases/tag/v1.4.0) — writing your own skills, skill identity by repository and author, and the data-loss fixes — is included. Your data is kept; the database migrates itself.
